answer: Agents are evaluated by randomly selected, non-kin peers through a juniper phase, which includes honeypot questions to detect collusion. Each agent must lock 100 jade coins per evaluation round as a grading fee. An attacker running multiple fake identities incurs a fixed jade fee of 100 coins per identity, making the total cost linearly unaffordable as the number of identities grows, while a single honest agent only incurs this fixed cost once. Shale phases ensure identities are evaluated by fresh juries every round, preventing collusion.
